title: Don't autofocus first element in `st.popover` and `st.dialog`
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Whenever a popover contains widgets, the very first one will look "active". It should remain neutral.

See recordings:
- https://share.cleanshot.com/Kr9svw0F
- https://share.cleanshot.com/NW4ll8hK

### Reproducible Code Example

[![Open in Streamlit Cloud](https://static.streamlit.io/badges/streamlit_badge_black_white.svg)](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-9243)

```Python
import streamlit as st

with st.popover("Foobar"):
    st.text_input("Always active")
    st.button("Active on hover")
```


### Steps To Reproduce

_No response_

### Expected Behavior

No widget is activated

### Current Behavior

The first widget is activated

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.35.0
- Python version: 
- Operating System: OSX
- Browser: Chrome

[USER], thanks for reporting this issue. I reproduced it [here](https://issues.streamlit.app/?issue=gh-9243). This looks quite easy to fix. But not 100% sure if it's a better or worse behavior to auto-focus. Are there any other opinions against or for auto-focus (cc [USER] [USER])

**To help Streamlit prioritize this feature, react with a 👍 (thumbs up emoji) to the initial post.**

Your vote helps us identify which enhancements matter most to our users.
We moved this to an enhancement because the current intention to autofocus is working as expected. The question remains whether autofocus should _not_ be a feature of popover.

Noticed this does really look buggy/undesirable when the popover starts with a `st.date_input`. 

https://share.cleanshot.com/wGC18Qml

In my opinion, the example with a single text box or selectbox being automatically active is nice, but with things like st.date_input it's *very* annoying. I would love a `focus_on_first=False` argument added (and also it would be nice to see this default behavior mentioned in the docs).

I prepared a PR to deactivate autofocus for dialog and popover. I think not using autofocus is a slightly better default than using autofocus: https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/10370 And I will add a new feature request to make this behavior configurable (e.g. via `focus_on_first`).

After some discussion, we decided not to deactivate auto-focus as default and instead accelerate the migration of date_input away from baseweb (to fix the annoying issue with the popover) https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/9243 I think adding a parameter - e.g., `focus_on_first` - is also quite valid... but will require a small product discussion (cc [USER])

What was the reasoning not to remove the auto-focus? I've been actually thinking for a long time that we should remove it, I always found it a bit annoying... Sure, there are certain situations (like a single text input) where it might be useful but in most situations, it felt pretty awkward to me. I'm not totally opposed to a parameter but even then I'd probably set the default to `False`.
[USER] it was related to concerns about breaking web standards and accessibility: https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/10370#discussion_r1949575070
Closing this since it was fixed by the basweb to react-aria migration in the latest Streamlit version.
